subject: Acme Commerce — sudden 429/5xx spike (retry storm)
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@acmecommerce.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Urgent: Sudden spike in 429/5xx after 05:50 deploy

Olga —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429 and a handful of 5xx errors in our production traffic starting at ~05:50 PT after the rollout of service v3.12. Error rate went from ~0.2% to 6.8% and user-facing latency spiked. Our front-end shows many repeated POSTs from the same clients (no client-side throttling). Attaching a short sample of logs and a screenshot of the dashboard.

We're under pressure from our ops team; can Redwood help triage and advise on immediate mitigations? We suspect a retry loop, but we need confirmation.

Thanks,
Helen Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Commerce

olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-28T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Sudden spike in 429/5xx after 05:50 deploy

Quick triage notes (initial):

- I looked through the attached logs. Pattern: repeated POSTs from identical client IPs and UA strings; timestamps show tight request loops (intervals of ~100ms). Many entries are 429 followed by immediate retries.
- Acme appears to be using our open-source client SDK v1.4.0; defaults in that version set maxRetries=5 and no jitter/backoff (linear immediate retry). The customer's deploy added a client-side bulk worker that replayed failed items without exponential backoff.
- On our side, the edge returned 429 for short windows (rate limit buckets hit) and several downstream inference workers returned 5xx under high concurrent KV cache load. We saw queue depth rise for one model shard.

Recommendations (immediate):
1) Ask Acme to flip their client SDK to enable exponential backoff + jitter (sample config attached). Also patch the worker to stop immediate replays. We can provide a short patch they can apply in <30m.
2) Apply an emergency soft-rate-limit on the Redwood edge for Acme's API key (throttle to 50 rps) to break the retry loop while they deploy the patch.
3) Shift a fraction of Acme traffic to a lower-concurrency model variant (degraded but more stable) while we drain queues.
4) Post-incident: recommend they upgrade to SDK v1.4.2 which includes safer retry defaults.

I will draft the quick mitigation steps for Olga to send to Acme.

—Monica
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): proposed-sdk-patch.diff
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@acmecommerce.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmecommerce.com>, monica.patel@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-28T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Action plan: short-term controls and SDK patch (Acme Commerce)

Helen —

Thanks for the logs. Monica's initial triage suggests your deployment's worker + SDK defaults are triggering a retry storm: immediate retries with no jitter are amplifying our rate limits and driving downstream 5xx. We propose the following immediate plan to stop user impact within the hour: 

1) Apply our emergency soft-rate-limit to your API key (we'll throttle to 50 rps effective in ~5 minutes). This is intended to break the retry loop so our backends can recover.
2) Please apply the attached SDK patch (proposed-sdk-patch.diff) or set SDK config: maxRetries=3, backoffBaseMs=100, maxBackoffMs=2000, jitter=true. Monica can push a one-line hotfix to your worker; ETA 20–30 minutes.
3) We will failover 20% of your traffic to model-b (lower concurrency) to reduce pressure on the shard showing queue growth.
4) After stabilization, we'll run a 1-hour soak and follow up with a short RCA and recommended long-term changes (upgrade to SDK v1.4.2, add client-side circuit breaker).

If you can confirm you will deploy the SDK change, we'll enact the edge throttle now. If you'd prefer, we can also temporarily disable retries server-side for your key.

Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
